sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Major discovery: Yl' has changed! It's now Y 45 [42,47,9,17] — the yellow piece has shrunk from 54 to 45 pixels, and its bounding box is now cols 9-17 (previously 9-20). The overlapping portion (cols 18-20, 3 columns × 3 rows = 9 cells… 54-45 = 9 ✓) has been consumed/erased!
So the mechanic is: when a black piece overlaps with a yellow piece, the overlapping yellow cells get erased (the piece "eats" the yellow, or the piece fuses and the yellow disappears). The piece stops when… hmm, BR stopped at cols 18-29 with 3 columns of overlap. Why did it stop there?
Looking at the display: rows 42-44: Y is at cols 9-17 (9 wide), then B is at cols 18-29. Rows 45-47: Y is at cols 12-17 (6 wide, the stub), B is at cols 18-29 (BR's bar? no wait).
Wait, BR = T-shape: bar (rows 42-44) + stub (rows 45-47). Display rows 42-44: '#########BBBBBBBBBBBB' = Y 9 + B 12. Rows 45-47: '......######...BBBBBB' = Y 6 (cols 12-17) + B 6 (cols 21-26). So BR's stub is at cols 21-26.
So the yellow's bar (originally cols 9-20) lost cols 18-20 (3 cells × 3 rows = 9). The yellow's stub (cols 12-17) is intact.
BR stopped when its bar had overlapped by 3 columns. Why 3? Maybe the piece moves until its leading edge aligns with…? Hmm. Or: the piece moves 3 cells per action, and the move is only allowed if the destination doesn't overlap with the yellow? BR at cols 21-32 (before the 8th LEFT): the 8th LEFT would put it at 18-29, overlapping the yellow's bar at 18-20. But that was allowed (9 yellow cells erased). The 9th LEFT would put it at 15-26, overlapping the yellow's bar at 15-17 (9 more cells) and the stub at… the stub is at cols 12-17, rows 45-47; BR's stub at rows 45-47 would be at cols 18-23 → no overlap with the stub (12-17). So the 9th would erase 9 more bar cells. But it stopped.
Maybe the rule is: the piece can erase at most 9 yellow cells per move? Or: the piece stops when the overlap exceeds a certain amount? Or: the piece stops when the yellow piece is…?
Or: the piece fuses with the yellow, and the fused shape must remain valid? Hmm.
Or: the piece moves 3 cells per action, but the move is blocked if the new position overlaps the yellow by more than 3 columns?
Let me think from another angle: maybe the goal is to erase all the yellow! The piece eats the yellow as it moves. Win = all yellow erased (or the piece fully covers it). In levels 1-2, the piece exactly covered the yellow (the yellow disappeared upon completion). Here, the yellow is larger than the piece's single-pass coverage, so the piece has to sweep across the yellow to erase it all!
BR (T, 48+6=54 cells) vs Yl' (54 cells): if BR exactly covers Yl', all 54 get erased. BR is currently overlapping by 9. To erase the rest, BR has to move further left — but it's blocked!
Why is it blocked? Maybe the piece can't move if the move would overlap with the yellow… but the 8th LEFT did overlap. Unless the 8th LEFT was the last allowed one because…?
Hmm wait, maybe I miscounted: BR started at cols 42-53. 11 LEFTs commanded. If each LEFT = 3 cols: after 8 LEFTs → 42-24=18 ✓ (cols 18-29). 9th → 15-26. What's at 15-17, rows 42-44? The yellow's bar (now 9-17). Overlap 15-17 = 3 cols. Plus the stub: BR's stub would be at cols 18-23, rows 45-47; the yellow's stub is at 12-17 → no overlap. So the 9th LEFT should erase 9 more cells. It didn't happen.
Maybe the rule is: the piece can erase yellow only if the yellow piece remains connected? After the 9th, the yellow's bar = 9-14 (6 wide) + stub 12-17 → still connected. Hmm.
Or: the piece stops when it has erased enough that the remaining yellow equals the piece's…? No, that's not it.
Let me test empirically: push LEFT once more and see what happens. Also try UP/DOWN to check if it's a directional issue.
Actually — wait. Maybe the piece is now "stuck" because the yellow has become an obstacle: the piece can erase on entry, but can't move while overlapping? I.e., a move is only allowed if the current position doesn't overlap the yellow? BR is currently overlapping (9 cells). So no moves allowed at all until it moves away? Test: LEFT, then RIGHT, then UP.
Let me probe: LEFT (expect: blocked or erases more), then RIGHT (expect: moves right, does the yellow get restored? or stays erased?).
